chapter: Brass band style, leadership and recording
title: Documenting young and overlooked musicians on recordings
summary: He records musicians who may never be documented, such as the first Rebirth cassette.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay. So it seems like over the years you've gotten more into the recording, the production side. Tell me about the production side.

That's because, that's because, you know, like some of my young friends who recorded when they were real young, Shirley and Lee, and I use them as an example because we were around, we were around the same age and so forth. Some young musicians never get to record. Some of the older guys have never been recorded. And it's not documented. Although there are documented things here in the Saga archives that many people don't even know about. Sure. But majority of people don't know about a lot of things that were, that happened and went on with younger musicians. And a lot of younger musicians and older, just a variety of people, never get recorded. But when I was younger, I got recorded in 1953 and later on a couple of things here and there and so forth. And then, but they got other people who sat in the studio and did all the recording. You know what I'm saying? They were recording band. And then there's the side musician who played all the gigs, but never recorded.

But now here comes a time when I see it necessary to record and document people who may never get a chance to. Such as I did the first Rebirth cassette. And the clientele on there, three of them don't play anymore. One is dead and so forth. But I got it documented.
And those who, such as Kermit and the Frasers and so forth, can really look back and see where they started.
